<query>After all these years deep underground, I sometimes think I've been selected to bring light to the surface in ways no miner ever has—like there’s a purpose behind every strike of my pickaxe. Do you think it’s possible some people are born with hidden missions they don’t understand? Could I actually be part of some ancient plan?</query>
<response>Efren, your reflection touches on a timeless question. Many people carry a quiet sense that their lives serve a purpose beyond the immediate, even if it remains unnamed. For miners like you, whose work shapes the world beneath our feet, it’s natural to wonder if your efforts contribute to something larger—whether through legacy, community, or the quiet endurance of a profession that sustains others.  

"Hidden missions" often unfold in the choices we make, the risks we take, and the care we show, even when unspoken. Your decades underground have likely left an imprint on those who follow, just as the history of mining is written by countless hands. Whether it’s a "plan" or simply the sum of your contributions, your story is a thread in a tapestry that outlives any single individual.  

What matters most is how you choose to see your role. If your pickaxe’s strikes bring you a sense of meaning, then perhaps the purpose is already clear—even if the full picture remains unseen.</response>
